espn-603993.headline: Ireland's back row is a hooker and a shortlist
beats: Ireland are without Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Garry Ringrose. Dan Sheehan, the captain and a hooker, played the full 80 at number 8 for Leinster against Munster in their absence. Ian Keatley thinks starting him there would be "a little too cute".

Argentina are thinner still. Santiago Carreras, 70 caps, and prop Thomas Gallo, 39, are out, and centre Santiago Chocobares is in doubt after a head knock. Carreras's place goes to Mateo Soler, whose Test debut came off the bench against Australia last month.

Argentina have gone four home games without a win since beating Wales in July. The best of them was a 28–28 draw with Australia, and the defeat by England was by seven. Ireland's last game was a 21–40 loss in New Zealand in July.
Ireland have been third in the world rankings every week since July. Lose here, by any margin, and France take the place, which is a lot to ask a borrowed number 8 to prevent.

espn-603994.headline: Italy are missing 17. South Africa can spare four.
beats: Gonzalo Quesada has 17 players unavailable and calls them fundamental to the group. South Africa have four World Cup winners injured, Etzebeth and Pollard among them, and six uncapped players in their squad.

The difference is what is left. Italy conceded 57 to Australia and 47 to New Zealand in July and are still waiting for a point. South Africa lead the table on points difference, and even a draw in Turin would drop them below New Zealand to second in the world.

Salmaan Moerat is recalled after his move to La Rochelle, and his last Test was against Italy in July 2025. Markus Muller, 19, is set to break a South African record of Frans Steyn's that has stood for 20 years.
South Africa won 32–14 the last time they came to Italy, on 15 November 2025. Turin is the audition. France away, six days later, is not.

espn-603995.headline: Thirty-three goes at New Zealand. Two draws, no wins
beats: Gregor Townsend lost 62-31 and 69-20 to them as a player. "As a player, I don't think we ever felt we could win the game," he says. As a coach he has lost three times to them in Edinburgh, by five, eight and eight.
Last November Scotland trailed 17-0 at Murrayfield, drew level at 17-17 and still lost 25-17. Townsend's own verdict is that the belief was there and the composure was not.

New Zealand put 50 and 43 on Australia in October after three straight defeats by South Africa. Dave Rennie is also looking into a growing list of lower-limb injuries. Win, and Scotland go up to fifth in the world, above England.
Fail, and the next attempt comes in Dunedin next year. Scotland's last match in New Zealand, in 2000, ended 48-14.

espn-603996.headline: One point in it last November, one point in it now
beats: Wales beat Japan 24–23 at home on 15 November 2025. In July that year Japan had won 24–19 in Kitakyushu, the defeat that stretched Wales' losing run to 18 Tests. Now Wales sit ninth in the Nations Championship, with Japan tenth and a point behind.

Wales have not played since July, when they lost 43–0 in South Africa without scoring a try. Japan beat Fiji 20–15 to win the Pacific Nations Cup in September. Fiji then beat them 34–28 in October, and Japan fell from ninth to twelfth in the world rankings.
Wales are the better-rested side. Japan are in better form, if not in rank. Win by any margin and Japan climb above Wales and Italy in the world rankings.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England. Neither will find the next one easier.

espn-603997.headline: Eleven men down, and France start with Fiji
beats: France were already missing seven, Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos among them, when four more withdrew. Antoine Hastoy's ankle is one of them, and Castres fly-half Louis Le Brun comes in uncapped.
Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship without a point. They come off a 34–28 win over Japan in Tokyo, a month after Japan beat them 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final.
Any defeat costs France fourth place in the world, with South Africa in six days later. Their last meeting with Fiji, on 15 November 2025, finished 34–21 to France at home.
Fiji appointed Jake White in October. His last Test job ended in France in 2007, with the World Cup.

espn-603998.headline: Battle-hardened, or just bruised by New Zealand
beats: Australia have played 10 Tests since July. England have played none since 18 July. Their preparation was a three-day camp at Bagshot before the players went back to their clubs, which Borthwick calls "doing more of less".

The hardening came at a price. Australia conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand on successive Saturdays, not long after beating South Africa 42–38. Les Kiss has since recalled Kurtley Beale, 37, five years after his last Test.

England's own plans hinge on Fin Smith's calf. He started at 10 in all three July Tests and is a doubt. England won 25–7 at home last November. Lose this time and Australia go fifth in the world, with England down to seventh, behind Scotland.
Warren Gatland says there is "a lot at stake" for Borthwick. Four months off against ten Tests of wear, and only one of them gets to call it an advantage.
